title: Grand classifier ALPHA raised 0.025 -> 0.05 corpus-wide, direct request (Hamm); omission_class O++ count moves 14->17 (FEF 5->6), reclassified without rerunning the 9,918s permutation stage
notes: Triggered by a fig03 panel-b/e/f review: Hamm expected ~20 O++ units total, 9 in FEF, which matched neither omission_class (v1, q<=.025 peak+ramp conjunction: 14 total, FEF=5) nor omission_class_v2 (q<=.025 peak-vs-competitor-epoch: 23 total, FEF=2). Tried several threshold variants against the existing q1_q/q1_ramp_q columns before asking Hamm to pick: uncorrected p<=.05 with ramp (18 total, FEF=6), q<=.05 with ramp (17 total, FEF=6), q<=.025/p<=.05 WITHOUT the ramp requirement (300+ total, FEF ~40 -- overshoots by an order of magnitude). Hamm confirmed q<=.05 with the existing peak+ramp conjunction ('this makes sense') despite it landing at FEF=6 not 9 -- accepted as close enough to the recollection, not an exact match.

IMPLEMENTATION: classify_omission_units_grand.py's module-level ALPHA constant changed 0.025->0.05 (affects every question: q1/omission_class, q1v2/omission_class_v2, q2/knows_when, q3/knows_what, q4/after_class -- all use the same ALPHA). Rather than rerunning that script's full permutation stage (1,000 shuffles x 9,056 units x 4 question families, 9,918s per its own receipt), wrote scripts/reclassify_omission_units_alpha.py: BH q-value columns (q1_q, q1_ramp_q, q2_q, q3_q, q4_q, q1v2_vs_pre_q, q1v2_vs_all_q) are a deterministic function of the raw p-values alone and do not depend on ALPHA, so only the final `<= ALPHA` threshold comparisons needed rerunning, not the permutation tests that produced the p-values. That script copies the classification block verbatim from the canonical script (byte-for-byte, explicitly flagged in its own docstring to stay in sync if that logic changes) and updates outputs/classification/omission_grand_units.csv in place plus outputs/classification/omission_grand_receipt.json's alpha_fdr/counts/counts_v2/knows_when/knows_what/after_counts fields (fig03_unit_census.py reads alpha_fdr from that receipt directly for its own panel-a stats, so leaving it stale would have desynced the receipt from the table it describes).

NEW CORPUS-WIDE COUNTS (9,056 units, 22 sessions): omission_class (v1) ns=8469 (was 8517), O+=320 (was 297), O-=241 (was 222), O++=17 (was 14), O--=9 (was 6). omission_class_v2: ns=7590 (was 7707), O+=1442 (was 1326), O++=24 (was 23). O++ by area (v1, new): FEF=6, PFC=3, V4=3, V1=2, V3a/d=2, TEO=1.

v1_vs_v2_crosstab in omission_grand_receipt.json is now STALE (computed at the old alpha) and was not regenerated by the reclassify script -- flagged in that receipt's own 'reclassified' block, not silently left wrong.
issues: Corpus-wide change: every script reading omission_class from outputs/classification/omission_grand_units.csv is now working from different classification labels than when its own outputs were last generated, if it ran before 2026-08-13T15:36. Checked which scripts consume it: scripts/extract_population_firing_lfp_power_corr.py reads omission_class directly to define the O-family for its LFP-power correlation output (feeds fig07, which per the 2026-08-12 handoff is in 'PPC audit only, no redesign' phase -- its existing extract outputs are now stale relative to the new classification but this was not rerun, since fig07 isn't being finalized this session). context/figures/fig02_spiking_exemplar_rasters/fig02_spiking_exemplar_rasters.py's O+ column exemplar pick (area=V4, ranked by |q1_effect_hz| among omission_class in {O+,O++}) could theoretically select a different top unit now that the candidate pool is looser -- not checked/rerun. fig02's O++ column is unaffected (hardcoded manual override unit, independent of omission_class). scripts/classify_omission_units_condition.py and scripts/classify_omission_units_jitter.py define their own separate, locally-scoped omission_class columns with their own ALPHA constants -- NOT consumers of the grand table, unaffected by this change (not independently re-verified that their local ALPHA is still 0.025, only confirmed they don't read the grand table).

The manuscript's stated FDR alpha for the O-family test family is now 0.05 where it may have been cited elsewhere (docs, prior figures' captions, PROJECT_STATE.md) as 0.025 -- not audited for stale mentions outside this classifier and fig03 in this pass.
plan: If fig07's PPC panels move from audit to design/render, rerun scripts/extract_population_firing_lfp_power_corr.py (and check extract_spike_lfp_coupling.py / extract_within_session_spk_spk_sliding_corr.py for the same dependency) against the reclassified table first.
If fig02 is revisited, re-check whether the O+/V4 exemplar pick changes under the new candidate pool.

Audit context/PROJECT_STATE.md and any figure caption text for a stale '0.025' FDR-alpha citation tied to the O-family classifier specifically (other alphas in the project, e.g. fig05's GLMM BH family, are unrelated and untouched).
